Best Movies of Robert Forster, Ranked

Discover Robert Forster's greatest performances, from his Oscar-nominated role in Jackie Brown to his early breakthrough in Medium Cool. Explore how this versatile actor brought authenticity and depth to every character across his six-decade career.

23 January 2025 · RewindZone Archive

Like many character actors who command the screen without commanding headlines, Robert Forster had that rare gift of making every film better just by showing up. I've spent countless hours revisiting his filmography, and what strikes me most is how he never phoned it in—not once, not ever. In ranking his 20 best performances, I've looked beyond just box office numbers or critical acclaim. Instead, I've considered how each role showcases his remarkable range, from subtle character studies to memorable supporting turns. Whether you're a long-time fan or just discovering his work, join me in celebrating an actor who understood that true screen presence isn't about stealing scenes—it's about making them real.

Here Are Our Final Rankings

20. Grand Theft Parsons (2004)

Advertisement

As Ralph Parsons, Forster brings understated humour and dignity to this offbeat true story about the theft of musician Gram Parsons' body. His performance helps anchor the film's more eccentric elements.

19. Stunts (1977)

In this thriller set against the backdrop of Hollywood's stunt industry, Forster plays Glen Wilson, a stuntman investigating his brother's suspicious death. His physical presence and dramatic intensity drive this underappreciated genre film.

18. The Don Is Dead (1973)

Early in his career, Forster demonstrated his talent for crime drama in this mob story. Though not the lead, his supporting performance shows the charisma that would define his later work.

17. 29th Street (1991)

This heartwarming comedy-drama features Forster in a supporting role that perfectly demonstrates his ability to bring authenticity to even smaller parts. His natural warmth shines through.

16. Human Nature (2001)

Advertisement

Charlie Kaufman's quirky script gives Forster a chance to showcase his rarely-seen comedic timing. His deadpan delivery provides some of the film's most memorable moments.

15. Diamond Men (2000)

Playing a veteran diamond salesman, Forster carries this quiet character study with subtle grace. His performance captures the dignity of a man facing professional and personal crossroads.

14. Automata (2014)

In this sci-fi noir, Forster plays a corporate executive navigating a world of artificial intelligence. His grounded performance helps sell the futuristic premise.

13. Ghosts of Girlfriends Past (2009)

As Sergeant Volkom, Forster provides a solid emotional anchor in this supernatural romantic comedy. His presence adds credibility to the fantastical elements.

12. The Wolf of Snow Hollow (2020)

One of his final roles sees Forster as Sheriff Hadley, bringing gravitas and humanity to this horror-comedy hybrid. His performance adds emotional depth to the genre elements.

11. The Stalking Moon (1968)

This tense western thriller showcases early career Forster at his best. His intense screen presence was already fully formed in this demanding role.

10. Original Gangstas (1996)

Forster shines in this urban action film, bringing his trademark intensity to a story of community justice. His performance elevates the material above standard genre fare.

9. Vigilante (1982)

As a factory worker turned vigilante, Forster delivers a powerful performance that balances rage with moral complexity. His work makes the character's transformation believable.

8. Rear Window (1998)

Taking on a role immortalised by James Stewart is no easy task, but Forster makes it his own in this TV remake. His interpretation brings fresh perspective to the classic thriller.

7. The Delta Force (1986)

Playing against type as the antagonist, Forster brings unexpected depth to what could have been a one-dimensional villain. His performance stands out even alongside Chuck Norris.

6. American Grindhouse (2010)

Though a documentary, Forster's narration proves essential to this exploration of exploitation cinema. His voice lends authority and authenticity to the subject matter.

5. The Black Hole (1979)

As Captain Dan Holland, Forster grounds Disney's ambitious sci-fi adventure. His serious approach helps sell the film's darker themes and spectacular visuals.

4. Alligator (1980)

This cult classic creature feature succeeds largely due to Forster's committed performance as Detective David Madison. He plays the material straight, making the outlandish premise work.

3. El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie (2019)

Forster's final role as Ed "The Disappearer" Galbraith showcases his mastery of subtle character work. His scenes provide some of the film's most compelling moments.

2. Medium Cool (1969)

This groundbreaking blend of fiction and reality features one of Forster's most important performances. As news cameraman John Cassellis, he navigates real-life chaos during the 1968 Democratic Convention with remarkable authenticity.

1. Jackie Brown (1997)

Forster's Oscar-nominated performance as Max Cherry represents the perfect marriage of actor and role. His portrayal of the world-weary bail bondsman who finds unexpected romance captures both strength and vulnerability. The chemistry with Pam Grier feels genuine, and every scene demonstrates why this role revitalised his career. It's a masterclass in understated acting that showcases everything that made Forster one of cinema's most reliable talents.

FAQ Section

What was Robert Forster's most acclaimed role?

Forster's portrayal of Max Cherry in Jackie Brown (1997) earned him an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor and is widely considered his finest performance.

When did Robert Forster start his acting career?

Forster began his film career in 1967, with his breakthrough role coming in 1969's Medium Cool.

What was Robert Forster's final film role?

His final appearance was as Ed "The Disappearer" Galbraith in El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie (2019), reprising his role from the Breaking Bad television series.

Which genres did Robert Forster work in most often?

While Forster worked across all genres, he was particularly known for his work in crime dramas, thrillers, and action films. He brought gravitas to every role, regardless of genre.

What made Robert Forster's acting style unique?

Forster was known for his naturalistic, understated approach to acting. He could convey complex emotions with minimal dialogue, relying on subtle facial expressions and body language.
